- **Isotretinoin (systemic)**: use the ingredient concept via `concept_ancestor` but exclude topical/vaginal forms. I'll use the ingredient and rely on drug_era, filtering to oral. Let me use the ingredient concept id and descendants, restricting to oral products.

Now the main cohort analysis. I'll build it as CTEs in a single query.

arguments.sql_query:
WITH oral_iso AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT ca.descendant_concept_id AS drug_concept_id
  FROM omop.concept_ancestor ca
  JOIN omop.concept c ON c.concept_id = ca.descendant_concept_id
  WHERE ca.ancestor_concept_id = 984232
    AND c.domain_id = 'Drug'
    AND (lower(c.concept_name) LIKE '%oral%' OR lower(c.concept_name) LIKE '%capsule%' OR lower(c.concept_name) LIKE '%tablet%')
),
iso_exp AS (
  SELECT de.person_id, de.drug_exposure_start_date AS start_date,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY de.person_id ORDER BY de.drug_exposure_start_date) AS rn,
         MIN(de.drug_exposure_start_date) OVER (PARTITION BY de.person_id) AS first_ever
  FROM omop.drug_exposure de
  JOIN oral_iso o ON o.drug_concept_id = de.drug_concept_id
),
new_starts AS (
  SELECT ie.person_id, ie.start_date
  FROM iso_exp ie
  JOIN omop.person p ON p.person_id = ie.person_id
  WHERE ie.rn = 1
    AND DATEDIFF(year, DATEFROMPARTS(p.year_of_birth, ISNULL(p.month_of_birth,7), 1), ie.start_date) BETWEEN 10 AND 19
)
SELECT COUNT(*) AS adolescent_new_starts,
       COUNT(DISTINCT person_id) AS distinct_persons
FROM new_starts;

  FROM iso_exp ie

  WHERE ie.rn = 1
    AND DATEDIFF(year, DATEFROMPARTS(p.year_of_birth, ISNULL(p.month_of_birth,7), 1), ie.start_date) BETWEEN 10 AND 19
),
alt_concepts AS (
  SELECT concept_id FROM (VALUES (3006923),(3027388),(3005755),(46236949),(3000784)) v(concept_id)
),
alt_meas AS (
  SELECT ns.person_id,
         m.value_as_number, m.range_high, m.measurement_date
  FROM new_starts ns
  JOIN omop.measurement m ON m.person_id = ns.person_id
  JOIN alt_concepts a ON a.concept_id = m.measurement_concept_id
  WHERE m.measurement_date >= ns.start_date
    AND m.measurement_date <= DATEADD(day, 90, ns.start_date)
    AND m.value_as_number IS NOT NULL
    AND m.range_high IS NOT NULL AND m.range_high > 0
),
flagged AS (
  SELECT person_id,
         MAX(CASE WHEN value_as_number > 2.0 * range_high THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS alt_gt2uln,
         MAX(CASE WHEN 1=1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS had_alt
  FROM alt_meas
  GROUP BY person_id
)

  (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM flagged) AS with_alt_test_in_90d,

The `value_as_number` is populated on concept 3006923 (the LOINC quantitative ALT) but `range_high` is essentially never populated there. The SNOMED "measurement" concept (4146380) has `range_high` but no value. So numeric ULN comparison isn't feasible per-row.

Two workable paths: (1) use the SNOMED qualitative concept **"Alanine aminotransferase above reference range" (4249568)** — but only 1 record; or (2) apply a **fixed pediatric ULN** to the quantitative values. Let me check the unit and value distribution to apply a sensible fixed ULN, and also check whether `range_high` ever co-occurs with a value.

         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY de.person_id ORDER BY de.drug_exposure_start_date) AS rn
  FROM omop.drug_exposure de JOIN oral_iso o ON o.drug_concept_id = de.drug_concept_id
),
new_starts AS (
  SELECT ie.person_id, ie.start_date FROM iso_exp ie JOIN omop.person p ON p.person_id = ie.person_id
  WHERE ie.rn = 1 AND DATEDIFF(year, DATEFROMPARTS(p.year_of_birth, ISNULL(p.month_of_birth,7), 1), ie.start_date) BETWEEN 10 AND 19
)
SELECT uc.concept_name AS unit, COUNT(*) AS n,
       MIN(m.value_as_number) AS min_v, AVG(m.value_as_number) AS avg_v,
       MAX(m.value_as_number) AS max_v,
       SUM(CASE WHEN m.range_high IS NOT NULL AND m.range_high>0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS n_with_rangehigh
FROM new_starts ns
JOIN omop.measurement m ON m.person_id = ns.person_id
  AND m.measurement_date >= ns.start_date AND m.measurement_date <= DATEADD(day,90,ns.start_date)
LEFT JOIN omop.concept uc ON uc.concept_id = m.unit_concept_id
WHERE m.measurement_concept_id = 3006923 AND m.value_as_number IS NOT NULL

ORDER BY n DESC;

Units are IU/L (equivalent). ALT values are consistent and lab `range_high` is never populated with a value, so I'll apply a fixed ULN. Standard adult ULN ≈ 40 IU/L, so 2× ULN = 80 IU/L. I'll compute the rate on that basis, and report using both a per-patient and denominator-of-tested view.

arguments.sql_query:
WITH oral_iso AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT ca.descendant_concept_id AS drug_concept_id
  FROM omop.concept_ancestor ca
  JOIN omop.concept c ON c.concept_id = ca.descendant_concept_id
  WHERE ca.ancestor_concept_id = 984232 AND c.domain_id = 'Drug'
    AND (lower(c.concept_name) LIKE '%oral%' OR lower(c.concept_name) LIKE '%capsule%' OR lower(c.concept_name) LIKE '%tablet%')
),
iso_exp AS (
  SELECT de.person_id, de.drug_exposure_start_date AS start_date,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY de.person_id ORDER BY de.drug_exposure_start_date) AS rn
  FROM omop.drug_exposure de JOIN oral_iso o ON o.drug_concept_id = de.drug_concept_id
),
new_starts AS (
  SELECT ie.person_id, ie.start_date FROM iso_exp ie JOIN omop.person p ON p.person_id = ie.person_id
  WHERE ie.rn = 1 AND DATEDIFF(year, DATEFROMPARTS(p.year_of_birth, ISNULL(p.month_of_birth,7), 1), ie.start_date) BETWEEN 10 AND 19
),
alt_pat AS (
  SELECT ns.person_id,
         MAX(CASE WHEN m.value_as_number > 80 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS gt2uln
  FROM new_starts ns
  JOIN omop.measurement m ON m.person_id = ns.person_id
    AND m.measurement_date >= ns.start_date AND m.measurement_date <= DATEADD(day,90,ns.start_date)
  WHERE m.measurement_concept_id = 3006923 AND m.value_as_number IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY ns.person_id
)
SELECT

## Answer

Among **1,800 adolescents (age 10–19) newly started on systemic (oral) isotretinoin**, an ALT elevation > 2× ULN within 90 days was recorded in **11 patients**.

| Denominator | Rate |
|---|---|
| All adolescent new starts (1,800) | **11 / 1,800 = 0.6%** |
| Only those with an ALT result in 90d (845) | **11 / 845 = 1.3%** |

**How this was defined**
- **New start**: first-ever oral isotretinoin exposure (capsule/tablet/oral descendants of ingredient `984232`); topical/vaginal forms excluded.
- **Adolescent**: age 10–19 at the start date.
- **ALT**: quantitative serum/plasma ALT (LOINC concept `3006923`), any result 0–90 days after start; the max per patient was used.
- **> 2× ULN**: values are in IU/L (≈ U/L) and the lab's own `range_high` was **not populated** in this dataset, so I applied a **fixed ULN of 40 IU/L → threshold 80 IU/L**. Only ~47% (845/1,800) had any ALT measured in the window.

**Caveats**
- The result is sensitive to the ULN assumption. Pediatric sex-specific ULNs are lower (~22–30 U/L for girls/boys), which would raise the count; using 80 IU/L is the conservative adult-based threshold.
- Because lab-specific reference ranges are missing, this is a fixed-cutoff approximation, not a true per-lab "> 2× ULN" flag.
- Only measured patients contribute; the true rate depends on which denominator you consider clinically relevant (the 1.3% "of those tested" figure is usually the more meaningful one).
